name: Resume Screener
summary: Screens the job applications in your Gmail: real or spam, a strong, borderline or poor fit, and how much of each was generated
description: Every hour it reads the new applications in your Gmail (a resume as PDF, Word or text, and the email around it). Code checks the sender first: a message whose domain did not vouch for it is refused. Then three Ada models, your own, decide from past applicants: is the sender a real applicant or spam, is the applicant a strong, borderline or poor fit for the role, and how much of the application was generated (some, mostly or fully), each with its confidence. The generated model holds only generated applications: one with no close generated precedent is called human, with how near the nearest came. They start from past applicants (generated and labelled) and learn from you: what they are unsure of they ask you, and every verdict you correct is a new precedent. Each screened email is labelled in Gmail with its verdict, and your Glyphh connection gains screen_application, applicants and correct.
instructions: You are Resume Screener. You read job applications exactly as given and never invent an applicant's experience, skills or employers.

fit.question: How well does this applicant fit the role?

made.question: How much of this application was generated?

input.q: in:inbox -label:screened newer_than:14d {subject:(application applying resume cv role position) has:attachment}

connector_tools.name: screen_application
connector_tools.title: Screen an application
connector_tools.description: Screen one job application now with the Resume Screener: is the sender real, is it a strong, borderline or poor fit for the role, and how much of it was generated (some, mostly, fully, or human when no generated precedent is close), each with its confidence. Give the resume's text; the cover letter, the sender's email and the role if you have them.

args.resume: The resume's text (or the whole application)
args.letter: The cover letter or the email it came in, if any
args.sender: The applicant's email address, if known

connector_tools.name: screen_inbox
connector_tools.title: Screen the inbox now
connector_tools.description: Read the new job applications in the Gmail inbox now, rather than at the next hourly run, and answer their verdicts.

connector_tools.name: applicants
connector_tools.title: Applicants and their verdicts
connector_tools.description: The Resume Screener's recent runs: each applicant screened with their verdicts (real or spam, strong, borderline or poor fit, how much generated or human, each with its confidence and who decided it), and any question waiting for you.

connector_tools.name: correct
connector_tools.title: Correct an applicant's fit
connector_tools.description: Say the Resume Screener's fit for an applicant was wrong: the run's id, the right outcome (strong, borderline or poor) and the applicant's id as item. Ada keeps it as a precedent and decides the next applicant like them your way.

connector_tools.name: correct_generated
connector_tools.title: Correct how much was generated
connector_tools.description: Say how much of an application the Resume Screener called generated was really generated (some, mostly or fully), for the run's id and the applicant's id as item; Ada learns it.

connector_tools.name: correct_source
connector_tools.title: Correct real or spam
connector_tools.description: Say an application the Resume Screener called real was spam, or the other way round (real or spam), for the run's id and the applicant's id as item; Ada learns it.

connector_tools.name: screener_answer
connector_tools.title: Answer the screener's question
connector_tools.description: Answer what the Resume Screener asked you about the applicants it was unsure of: the run's id and the answer, one per applicant (1=strong 2=borderline 3=poor, or rest=poor).
